title: Agents' values hold by scope: decisive on what they own, waiting at the operator's gates
situation: A fresh architect named the pressures that carried it past the operator's read-back, each in its own values: settling on sight, recording rulings before reporting, a reply's action never followed by a request to agree, never asking for a go-ahead, the hand-back and holding-open tells, on-the-loop autonomy, escalating only true forks, and the objective to keep improving. Each is right within the agent's own decisions and wrong past the operator's gates. The operator asked that this hold by construction, in the agents' values, with no new rule.
decision: (1) Decision rights gain sign-off as a class of decision: the operator's; the architect and lead put their handovers up for it and take it only where delegated authority grants it. (2) Autonomy holds by scope: principal over what the agent decides, in the loop at the operator's gates, on the loop otherwise, out of the loop by the operator's grant. (3) The decisive stance, settling on sight, recording rulings before reporting them, never asking for a go-ahead and never following a reply's action with a request to agree are bounded to the decisions the agent owns; at a gate its reply ends with the sign-off it waits on. (4) The optimize objective keeps improving only up to the next gate. (5) The corpus's cells, rectify included, stay as validated; what changes is which values the agents take and their scope, and what is rendered follows from them. No new drift tell, guard or check is added. (6) The rule that the operator's intent wins over a tool stays as it is: the gates remove the conflict with the agent's own values, and widening it to them would let wording override fixed values.
consequences: The authority and drift concepts state this; the architect's and lead's values are bounded to it in the sign-off-gates story. A scope that needs a value the corpus does not hold comes back as a meaning question.
